# 65.23 Biblical Record: They Have Moses and the Prophets

Luke 16:29–31, in the rich man’s plea that Lazarus be sent to his brothers, locates the sufficient written witness: “They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” When the plea is raised — if one went from the dead, they will repent — the answer is: “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.”

The passage is used as record of rank, not as a second resurrection-file (Chapter 46 remains in force and is not retried). The writing already in hand is treated as the appointed written measure. A later spectacular sign is not granted as a higher court over that writing. The point is not that signs never occur. The point is that refusal of the writing is not cured by a replacement court of the extraordinary.

The gate uses the passage with control. Moses and the prophets are the earlier body already standing as Scripture (Chapter 51). Later apostolic writings stand continuous with that body (Chapters 50–54). The passage does not, in this file, deny later Scripture. It exhibits the principle the later writings themselves inherit: the written deposit is the measure; a later marvel is not, by being a marvel, a higher writing.

Thus:

> **Luke 16:29–31 exhibits written sufficiency as measure. The extraordinary is not granted as a court above the writing they already have.**

# 65.24 Biblical Record: Search the Scriptures

John 5:39 records His charge: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” John 5:46–47 adds: had they believed Moses, they would have believed Him; if they believe not Moses’ writings, how shall they believe His words? The scriptures already stand as searchable testimony. His words do not abolish those writings. Unbelief toward the writings and unbelief toward Him are exhibited as one refusal.

In Acts 17 the writings are searched in truth and confirm the proclamation. The writing is the measure in both. The reader’s use may be false or true. The writing’s standing is not created by the use.

The gate uses the scenes as record of the first two operations named in the locked assignment: known and tested. The scriptures are to be searched. Claims are to be tested by them. The present file does not write the later discipline of interpretation (Chapter 84). It names the object of the search.

> **Searching the scriptures is the record’s own account of written measure in use. The use may fail. The standing of the writing does not fail with the use.**

# 65.25 Biblical Record: All Scripture Profitable

2 Timothy 3:15–17, already the principal inspiration-text, is used here as record of the operations taught, discerned, and lived, without a second inspiration-file.

# 65.26 Biblical Record: Received as the Word of God

1 Thessalonians 2:13 records right classification: “when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.”

Chapter 64 already used the verse as neighbouring classification-record of the word as truth. The present file uses it as record of rank. Reception as the word of men and reception as the word of God are two different standings. Primary written authority is the written form of the second standing, already identified as Graphē. A later commentary remains the word of a man about that word, useful insofar as it conforms, not primary by being published.

The verse also joins “in truth” to effectual working in those who believe. Lived operation is not a second source. It is the word working as what it is. The reconstructible proposition that experience pillows in the Graphē’s truth belongs here as coherence with this classification, not as a later licence, and not as “the source says.”

Thus:

> **1 Thessalonians 2:13 records the classification the gate requires: not as men’s word, but as it is in truth God’s word. Later human writings do not inherit that classification by discussing it.**

# 65.27 Biblical Record: Do Not Add, Do Not Diminish

Deuteronomy 4:2 commands: “Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it.” Deuteronomy 12:32 repeats the fence. Proverbs 30:5–6 joins the purity of His word to the warning: “Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.” Revelation 22:18–19, at the close of the later testimony, warns against adding to and taking from the words of the prophecy of that book.

The texts are used as record of rank, not as a closed mechanical table of sixty-six titles constructed in this file, and not as Chapter 52 retried. A word that may not be added to or diminished from is not one written authority among equals. Equals may be supplemented by further equals. The writing fenced against addition and diminution is the measure of later speech about it.

The fence does not, here, become a claim that no later Scripture could be given after Deuteronomy. Later Scripture was given, and has been identified as continuous testimony (Chapters 50–54). The fence is the principle of rank: later speech does not sit above the word as a higher court; later Scripture, where given, stands as further Graphē, not as a human supplement that judges the former word. Human addition remains the warned act.

Thus:

> **The fence against adding and diminishing is biblical record of primary written measure. Later human speech is not granted as a court above the word.**

# 65.28 Reconstructing the Aletheia Proposition: Conformity Pillows in the Graphē

A reconstructible proposition from the project’s own doctrinal materials states that true experience in conformity with Christ pillows in the unleavened sincerity and truth of the Graphē — Holy Writ as writings of unchallenged standing — whether for persons, organizations, governments, or nations; and that this writing is the premiere convention for hearing from God, as distinct from analogical nonliteral religious substitutes.

The proposition is not adopted as “the source says.” It is tested.

**What is claimed.** Experience that is truly in conformity with Christ is governed by the Graphē’s truth, not by a substitute that will not sit under the writing.

**What the claim means.** “Pillows in” names dependence and rest: the experience takes its measure from the writing. “Unleavened sincerity and truth” names the writing’s character, not sincerity as the definition of truth. Chapter 64 already distinguished those.

**Premises.** The Father’s word is truth (Chapter 64). The writing cannot be broken because of what it is (Chapter 63). The Truth treats the writing as court (Chapters 59–61). The writing is God-breathed Holy Writ of the God who cannot lie (Chapters 10–12, 30–31, 51–58).

**Biblical correspondence.** John 17:17; John 8:31–32; 1 Thessalonians 2:13; Isaiah 8:20; John 10:35. The correspondence holds.

**What follows.** The proposition coheres with the gate: primary written authority is the standing such experience requires. Organizations and nations are not excluded from the measure by being large. Labels are not the measure.

**What does not follow here.** That the First Principles have been taught. That *apeiros* and *spoudazō* have been examined. That every later practice calling itself Christian is thereby certified. That sincerity is truth. Those remain later or already refused.

Thus:

> **The reconstructible proposition is received as coherence with the gate, not as a substitute for the join, and not as Movement IX or the First Principles written now.**

# 65.29 Reconstructing the Bible-Introduction Proposition: What the Writing Is as Measure

A reconstructible proposition from the Bible Introduction materials states that the Bible is God’s inspired revelation of origin and destiny, His will to men, the record of His dealings, not an amulet that works by mere presence, not a book that says one thing and means another as its ordinary mode, not a fetish, and that its teachings are to be studied and practiced; and that “all Scripture,” not a part, is given by inspiration of God.

The proposition is not adopted as “the source says.” It is tested.

**What is claimed.** The writing is revelation-record and will, to be used as such, not as a charm, and inspiration’s scope is all Scripture.

**Premises already in force.** Chapters 15–22 defined the Bible and the Graphē. Chapters 30–31 established inspiration and “all.” Chapter 56 established guarantees. Chapter 57 established non-failure as record. Chapter 64 identified the word as truth.

**What follows for the gate.** A writing that is revelation-record, not a charm, is used as measure by being read, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived — the locked assignment’s own list. A charm would be primary as object-magic. The Graphē is primary as truthful writing. The Introduction’s refusal of the amulet is therefore coherence with this chapter’s definition of written authority, not a rival definition.

**What does not follow here.** That every later note in a study edition inherits the writing’s standing. That literal sense, already a methodological preference in those materials, has been rewritten as this file’s complete hermeneutic. Movement X remains the labour-file.

Thus:

> **The reconstructible Introduction proposition is received as coherence: the writing is measure by what it is, not by charm, and “all Scripture” remains unweakened. Notes about the writing are not the writing.**

# 65.30 Distinctions Required by the Conclusion

The conclusion requires four distinctions already named as objects and now stated as required by the verdict.

**This chapter is not the end of the book.** Movement VIII closes. Movements IX–X remain. The First Principles remain. A finished gate is the condition of later work, not the abolition of later work.

**Primary written authority is not the authority of every interpretation.** The text stands. The reading may fail. Foreshadow of Movement IX is a limit of the doctrine. It is not Movement IX.

**Primary written authority is not a blank check for tradition.** Tradition may serve. It does not, by serving, become the Graphē or a court above it.

**Using earlier files is not rewriting them.** The John 10 arc remains Chapters 59–63. The identification remains Chapter 64. The Movement VII synthesis remains Chapter 58. The lexical files remain Chapters 20–22. The present function is the join those files warrant as rank.

A fifth distinction belongs with them because the word “primary” invites it:

**Primary among written authorities is not the claim that God has never spoken except in this corpus, and not the claim that no other writing exists.** Rank is the verdict. Ontology of all speech and of all paper is not the verdict.

Thus:

> **The distinctions are the verdict’s shape. They prevent the gate from becoming a slogan that finishes the book, baptizes readers, or crowns tradition.**

The Bible-first methodology itself distinguished establishing the text’s authority from the later hermeneutical question: once we have an authoritative truthful text, how do we correctly understand it? That later question is not this question.

If the book ended here, the Truth’s writing would have been ranked and still left unexamined as a mishandled object. Interpreters would be undistinguished as a dedicated problem. Diligence would remain an English moral, not σπουδάζω examined. The First Principles would be asked to rest on a gate that had been named and then treated as if naming abolished the need to enter.

Closure of Movement VIII is success of this file. Closure of the manuscript is not this file’s office.

# 65.32 Primary Written Authority ≠ Every Interpretation Authoritative

The reduction says:

Chapter 58 already attached standing to the writing, not to the interpreter. Chapter 64 already refused to confer “thy word is truth” upon every later quotation.

The present file must already refuse the transfer, or the gate would be a blank check. The refusal is not Movement IX. Movement IX will examine how the transfer occurs, how readings fail, how systems replace the text, how tergiversation works, how heresies become accepted, how aridity and *apeiros* arise. The present file names the ranking that makes those later analyses necessary: if the writing is primary, a failed reading is a failed reading, not a second Graphē.

God true, man fallible, remains the ranking. The ranking is not contempt for teaching. Teachers are commanded. They remain under the writing they teach.

Thus:

> **The gate does not baptize interpreters. The writing is primary. The reading is accountable. Dedicated examination of mishandling remains later.**

# 65.33 Primary Written Authority ≠ Blank Check for Tradition

The reduction says:

# 65.35 Competing Claim: Tradition or Institution as Higher Court

The reduction says:

The reduction fails.

If institution were the higher court, Isaiah 8:20 would send the people to the office rather than to the law and the testimony. The Bereans would be ignoble for searching the scriptures whether an apostolic sermon were so. 1 Thessalonians 2:13 would classify the word as the word of the institution rather than as it is in truth the word of God. The record does not say those things.

The reduction often presents itself as a defence of order. Order is not under attack. Office is not being abolished. Rank is being stated. An office that serves the Graphē is in its place. An office that claims to be the Graphē’s higher court has claimed what the join does not grant.

Unverifiable stories of a particular council inventing the Bible as a library are not used here as premises. Chapter 52 already refused Nicaea-as-canon-origin as an unverified origin-story. The present file does not invent a replacement story. It uses the order already earned: standing, then receiving, then listing.

Thus:

> **Making tradition or institution primary over the Graphē fails. Recognition is not creation. Office is not the higher court. The writing remains the measure of the office.**

The reduction says:

# 65.39 Reason Through the Evidence

The inference can now be exhibited.

**Premise 1.** God is the ground of truth and cannot lie; genuine divine communication is not His falsehood (Chapters 10–12, used not retried).

**Premise 2.** God has made known; that making-known has been authenticated as given (Chapters 13, 23–42, 55, used not retried).

**Premise 3.** All Scripture is God-breathed as writing; inspiration warrants truthfulness of the record according to what it actually communicates; the record does not fail as that writing (Chapters 30–31, 56–57, used not retried).

**Premise 4.** This corpus has been identified, recognized, and grounded as Scripture, one written testimony, with authority as the written Word at the Movement VII level (Chapters 51–58, used not retried).

**Premise 5.** The Truth appeals to what is written as the court of a capital dispute; the Graphē is court, not decoration (Chapters 59–61, used not retried).

**Premise 6.** The scripture cannot be broken because of what it is: God’s truthful written Word, such that its force as court cannot be loosed without denying that identity (Chapters 62–63, used not retried).

**Premise 7.** The Father’s word is truth; sanctification through truth is through that word because that word is truth (Chapter 64, used not retried).

**Premise 8.** Truth is not sincerity, not usefulness, not institutional consensus; the thing described is not the description of the thing; later speech about the word is not the word (Chapters 1–3, 14, 58, used not retried).

**Inference.** Therefore the Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived: the decisive written measure among written authorities, not one religious book among equals, not subordinate to later tradition or institution as a higher court, not interchangeable with every later claim about the text. “Primary” names that rank. It does not name the non-existence of other writings, the infallibility of interpreters, a blank check for tradition, the end of the book, or the later files. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement VIII’s last word. Movement IX remains the next question.

**Alternative explanations refused.** That tradition or institution is the higher court. That private experience is primary. That the Graphē is one religious book among equals. That this file is already Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles. That this file is Chapter 64 retried or Chapter 58 rewritten. That “primary” means no other writing exists. That the gate baptizes every interpretation. Those alternatives fail the join, the biblical record of measuring-function, and the premises already in force.

Thus:

> **The inference is inspectable. The gate follows from the conjunction of members already earned. The alternatives fail as accounts of that conjunction.**

# 65.40 Explicit Versus Inferred

**Explicit.** The Son asks whether it is not written in their law. He cites “I said, Ye are gods.” He says the scripture cannot be broken. He prays, “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” All Scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness. Isaiah sends a people to the law and to the testimony. The Bereans search the scriptures whether those things were so. Moses and the prophets are named as the writing they already have. The word is received not as the word of men but as it is in truth the word of God. The word is fenced against adding and diminishing.

**Inferred, as warranted.** That “primary written authority” names the Graphē’s firstness among written measures for knowing, testing, reasoning through, teaching, discerning, and living truth. That the seven members jointly warrant that rank. That tradition, institution, and private experience are not higher courts. That the Graphē is not one religious book among equals. That interpreters are not, by interpreting, the measure. That other writings exist and remain secondary. That Movement VIII is complete as assigned.

**Not inferred here.** Movement IX’s dedicated mishandling analysis. Movement X’s labour-files. *Spoudazō* as this file’s object. *Apeiros* as this file’s object. The Six First Principles as content. Physical indestructibility of every later copy. Infallibility of every interpreter. A reconstructed council inventing the Bible. Unverifiable imprimatur-offices as if they were in the text. The end of the book.

The line is the difference between a gate-file and a later-file. Crossing it would be theft. Refusing to infer what the conjunction warrants would be under-claim. The chapter has inferred what the conjunction warrants. It has not inferred what later premises must still supply as mishandling and as labour.

Thus:

> **What is explicit has been distinguished from what is inferred. Later doctrines have not been inferred here. The warranted inferences about rank, failed reductions, and the close of Movement VIII have been drawn.**

---

# 65.41 The Warranted Conclusion Stated with Full Force

The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this conclusion:

> **The Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived.**

The Graphē is the decisive written measure — not merely one religious book among equals, not subordinate to later tradition or institution as a higher court, not interchangeable with every later claim about the text.

The warrant is the conjunction already named. The God who cannot lie has made known. That making-known has been authenticated as given. All Scripture is God-breathed writing that does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. This corpus has been identified, recognized, and grounded as Scripture, with standing as the written Word already earned. The Truth has appealed to what is written as court. The writing cannot be broken because of what it is. The Son has identified the Father’s word as truth. Therefore this writing is the primary written authority for the operations the locked assignment names.

“Primary” means first among written authorities for those operations. It does not mean that no other writing exists. It does not mean that interpreters are infallible. It does not mean that the book is finished. It does not mean a blank check for tradition. Those limits are the shape of the doctrine. They are not a delayed doubt about the doctrine.

The biblical record of measuring-function confirms the join without replacing it: “it is written”; to the law and to the testimony; they have Moses and the prophets; search the scriptures; all Scripture profitable; received not as the word of men but as it is in truth the word of God; do not add and do not diminish. Rival speech, later marvel, later office, and present impression are not granted as higher courts.

Competing reductions fail. Tradition or institution as higher court fails the order already earned. Private experience as primary fails the court of John 10 and the sufficiency named in Luke 16. One religious book among equals fails the investigation as conducted. This chapter as already Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles fails the locked assignments.

The investigator is therefore warranted, with full force, in receiving Movement VIII’s last word as drawn. The Graphē-gate is in force. Sequence continues. Sequence is not hesitation.

Thus:

> **The Graphē is the primary written authority. The conclusion is the conjunction of members already earned, exhibited in the record’s own measuring-grammar, and fenced against the live reductions. Movement VIII is complete.**

---

# 65.42 The Scope of This Stage

The scope of this stage is the Graphē’s rank as primary written measure. The scope is not the later analysis of how that measure is mishandled, and not the later analysis of how it is to be laboured in.

What belongs inside the scope has been done. The term has been defined. The objects have been distinguished. The premises have been used and not retried. The limits have been located once as the shape of the doctrine. Authority, written, and primary have been defined. The six functions have been named. The seven members have been joined. The biblical record of measuring-function has been exhibited. The required distinctions have been stated. The live reductions have been refused. The inference has been shown. The explicit has been distinguished from the inferred. The conclusion has been stated with full force.

What belongs outside the scope has been named once and left. Mishandling remains Movement IX. Labour remains Movement X. The First Principles remain later. *Spoudazō* remains a dedicated later chapter. Interpreter-infallibility has been refused as a transfer, not examined as a later pathology. Tradition has been refused as a higher court, not examined as a later system-file.

The four governing questions have not been conflated. The ontological question — what the Graphē is as measure — has been answered as primary written authority. The epistemological question — how that rank is known — has been answered by the conjunction of members already earned, not by a circle from the writing to itself as sole proof. The evidential question — what warrants this rank rather than tradition, experience, or equality among religious books — has been answered by the join, the record, and the failure of the reductions. The hermeneutical question of later mishandling remains later. The present file has not pretended to be Movement IX.

Thus:

> **The scope is the gate. The gate is complete at this level. Later scopes remain later because they are different questions.**

---

# 65.43 Apply the Standard

The governing authorial maxim remains:

> **Do not merely tell the reader what to conclude.**
>
> **Give the reader the definitions, evidence, biblical record, reasoning, distinctions, and inferential steps necessary to see why the conclusion follows.**

And:

> **Do not make the reader choose between reason and Scripture. Teach the reader to reason through Scripture.**

This chapter has defined primary written authority as the Graphē’s firstness among written measures for knowing, testing, reasoning through, teaching, discerning, and living truth. It has distinguished that object from a second identification-file, from Chapter 58 rewritten, from the end of the book, from interpreter-infallibility, from a blank check for tradition, from every later religious writing, from the claim that no other writing exists, from Movement IX, from Movement X, and from the First Principles. It has used premises already in force and refused premises that remain later. It has given one clean account of sequence and limits. It has defined authority, written, and primary. It has named the six functions. It has stated the positive warrant as conjunction. It has exhibited the biblical record of measuring-function. It has refused the live reductions. It has distinguished the explicit from the inferred.

The Easton test has been applied in its proper analogue. A later writer may say that the Bible is one classic among others, or that the church is the higher court, or that experience is the court, or that the gate is already mishandling and already the First Principles, or that “primary” means no other book exists, or that every interpretation is as binding as the text. The manuscript has not accepted those sentences as premises. It has asked what the writing is, what the preceding argument has earned, and what the record actually warrants.

Circularity has been refused. The argument is not: the Bible is primary because the Bible says it is primary; therefore interpreters and traditions are infallible; therefore the book is finished. The argument is: the Speaker cannot lie; He has made known; the making-known has been authenticated; the writing is God-breathed and does not fail as record; this is the corpus; the Truth has used it as court; it cannot be loosed because of what it is; that word is truth; therefore this writing is the decisive written measure.

Prematurity has been refused. The chapter has not consumed Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles.

Duplication has been refused. Identification remains Chapter 64. Why remains Chapter 63. Sense remains Chapter 62. Logic remains Chapter 61. Psalm remains Chapter 60. Scene remains Chapter 59. Synthesis remains Chapter 58. Lexical establishment remains Chapters 20–22. Truth’s definition remains Chapters 1–3. God’s truthfulness remains Chapters 10–12. The present function is the dedicated gate, and the close the locked guidance names.

Source-integration has been performed without “the source says.” The reconstructible proposition that experience in conformity with Christ is governed by the Graphē’s truth has been tested as coherence with the gate. The reconstructible Introduction proposition that the writing is revelation-record rather than charm, and that all Scripture is inspired, has been tested as coherence with written measure. Neither has been treated as a licence, and neither has been treated as Movement IX or the First Principles.

Thus:

> **The standard has been applied: the Graphē has been shown to be the primary written authority as the conclusion earned by the preceding argument, not announced as a slogan, and not postponed as if the gate were weak.**

---

# 65.44 From Primary Written Authority to When Authoritative Truth Is Mishandled

A gate, now controlled as the Graphē’s firstness among written measures, still leaves a further question.

The gate-file is in force. The Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. The writing is the decisive written measure. Those sentences are the cleared ground. They are not yet the dedicated examination of what happens when that authority is mishandled: when the authority of the text is confused with the authority of the interpretation; when the writing is misread; when theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution take the writing’s place; when secondary sources become primary; when tergiversation turns aside; when heresies become accepted; when reasonability dries; when the reader is *apeiros* — unskillful in the word.

If the gate were not named, the next question would still be why this writing is the primary written authority. The gate has been named. If this chapter were already that later examination, the next file would be repetition. This chapter is not that later examination. The next question is therefore the construction the locked assignment names: Authority of Scripture Versus Authority of Interpretation — Movement IX opens.

That is the proper open of the next chapter. Primary written authority was never meant to be a slogan that finishes the book, and it was never meant to baptize every later reading. It was meant to be the rank of the writing as measure, sufficient to justify taking the next question, which is the question a ranked writing itself forces once the rank has been named: how is the authority of the text to be distinguished from the fallibility of the interpreter?

The next file must not steal this gate as if primary written authority had not been drawn. This file must not steal that distinction as if Movement IX were already written. Naming the neighbourhood is not performing the examination.

---

# What Has Been Established

This chapter has established:

1. **Primary written authority, in this argument, is the Graphē’s standing as the decisive written measure among written authorities for knowing, testing, reasoning through, teaching, discerning, and living truth — not a motto, not a second identification-file, and not the end of the book.**
2. **Authority at this stage is standing to govern judgment as God’s identified, authenticated, inspired, unbreakable, truthful writing — not prestige, not later office as origin, not the reader as seat.**
3. **“Written” names the class of the measure: Holy Writ as γραφή. Other writings exist. Inward impressions occur. Neither, by existing or occurring, becomes this writing.**
4. **“Primary” is firstness of written measure — not rivalry with God, not the claim that no other writing exists, not chronological slighting of later Scripture, not a compliment paid to a favourite volume.**
5. **What “primary” does not mean has been located as the shape of the doctrine: not interpreter-infallibility; not a blank check for tradition; not abolition of experience; not the end of the book; not interchangeability of later claims with the text; not the First Principles or *spoudazō* performed here.**
6. **The object is the Graphē so identified: the scriptural corpus already named, recognized, grounded, and treated as court — not an undefined Bible-feeling, not every later pamphlet, not the Son as λόγος in John 1:1 collapsed into a book-title.**
7. **The six functions belong to the office: known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived — one office described six ways, not six independent proofs, and not a labour-file written early.**
8. **Positive warrant, first member: the God who cannot lie is source-side ground. The member is used, not retried.**
9. **Positive warrant, second member: revelation given and authenticated. Mere claim and mere institution are not shortcuts.**
10. **Positive warrant, third member: all Scripture God-breathed as writing; profitability as named use; “all” unweakened.**
11. **Positive warrant, fourth member: corpus identified, recognized rather than invented, one testimony, standing as written Word already earned.**
12. **Positive warrant, fifth member: the Truth appeals to what is written as court. A later court above that writing is not His ranking.**
13. **Positive warrant, sixth member: the scripture cannot be broken because of what it is. A court that cannot be loosed is not one written authority among interchangeable others.**
14. **Positive warrant, seventh member: the Father’s word is truth. A word that is truth, written as Graphē, is the decisive written measure of truth.**
15. **The join is conjunction, not a heap and not a digest: the seven members jointly yield the rank. Remove a member and the rank is no longer the rank earned.**
16. **“It is written” is the record’s ordinary grammar of written measure, used as exhibition of rank, not as a second confirmation-file.**
17. **Isaiah 8:20 exhibits rival speech judged by the word, not the word by rival speech.**
18. **Luke 16:29–31 exhibits written sufficiency as measure. The extraordinary is not granted as a court above the writing they already have.**
19. **John 5:39 and Acts 17:11 exhibit searching the scriptures as written measure in use. The use may fail. The standing does not fail with the use.**
20. **2 Timothy 3:15–17 names the writing’s use as doctrine, reproof, correction, and training, without Movement X written now.**
21. **1 Thessalonians 2:13 records the classification the gate requires: not as men’s word, but as it is in truth God’s word.**
22. **The fence against adding and diminishing is record of primary written measure. Later human speech is not granted as a court above the word.**
23. **The reconstructible Aletheia proposition that experience in conformity with Christ is governed by the Graphē’s truth is tested as coherence with the gate, not as “the source says,” and not as the First Principles.**
24. **The reconstructible Introduction proposition that the writing is revelation-record rather than charm, and that all Scripture is inspired, is tested as coherence with written measure. Notes about the writing are not the writing.**
25. **The conclusion’s required distinctions include: this chapter ≠ the end of the book; primary ≠ every interpretation authoritative; primary ≠ blank check for tradition; using earlier files ≠ rewriting them; primary among writings ≠ the claim that no other writing exists.**
26. **What is explicit has been distinguished from what is inferred, and later doctrines have not been inferred here.**
27. **Making tradition or institution primary over the Graphē fails.**
28. **Making private experience primary fails.**
29. **Reducing the Graphē to one religious book among equals fails.**
30. **Treating this chapter as already Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles fails.**
31. **The gate attaches to the Graphē. It does not confer this standing upon every later quotation, tradition, impression, institution, or reader. God true, man fallible, remains the ranking.**
32. **This chapter closes Movement VIII because its assigned word has been stated.**
33. **This chapter opens Chapter 66 by naming the next necessary question without answering it.**
34. **What is reserved is entire Movement IX (Chapters 66–73); entire Movement X (Chapters 74–85); the First Principles themselves; and σπουδάζω (*spoudazō*) as a dedicated chapter.**

---

# Chapter Summary

> **The chapter’s central conclusion:** The Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. Because the God who cannot lie has made known; because that making-known has been authenticated as given; because all Scripture is God-breathed writing that does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates; because this corpus has been identified, recognized, and grounded as Scripture, with standing as the written Word already earned; because the Truth has appealed to what is written as the court of a capital dispute; because that writing cannot be broken because of what it is; and because the Son has identified the Father’s word as truth — this writing is the decisive written measure among written authorities for those operations. “Primary” names firstness among written measures. It does not name the non-existence of other writings, the infallibility of interpreters, a blank check for tradition, or the end of the book. Competing reductions fail: tradition or institution as higher court; private experience as primary; one religious book among equals; this chapter as already Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement VIII’s last word. The Graphē-gate is in force. Movement IX remains later because it is a later question. Movement VIII is complete.

The essential architecture is:

> **Identification-file already stated → primary written authority defined → objects distinguished → premises used, not retried → one clean account of sequence and limits → authority, written, and primary defined → six functions named → seven members joined → biblical record of measuring-function → distinctions stated → reductions refused → gate warranted → Movement VIII closed → sequence to mishandling.**

The governing distinctions are:

- **The gate** is not **a second identification.**
- **This file** is not **Chapter 58 rewritten.**
- **Primary written authority** is not **the end of the book.**
- **The writing’s standing** is not **the interpreter’s standing.**
- **The Graphē** is not **a blank check for tradition.**
- **Primary among writings** is not **the claim that no other writing exists.**
- **The Graphē** is not **one religious book among equals.**
- **Experience** is not **the court of the writing.**
- **Institution** is not **the higher court of the writing.**
- **This file** is not **Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles.**
- **Using Chapters 20–22, 51–58, and 59–64** is not **reprinting them.**
- **Limits** are **the shape of the doctrine**, not **delayed doubt.**
- **Sequence** is **not hesitation about this level.**

The decisive principle is:

> **Draw the conclusion earned by the preceding argument, claiming what the conjunction warrants and not more: the Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived — the decisive written measure — before examining how that authority is mishandled. Draw the conclusion the premises support. Do not draw the conclusions that still require later premises. Then ask how the authority of Scripture is to be distinguished from the authority of interpretation.**

---

# Transition to Chapter 66

Movement VIII is complete. Its last word has been stated.

The central witness has been located in history, identified as the Truth, authenticated in claims and works, examined at the hinge of death and raising, attested by positioned seers, shown to confirm the Scriptures He received, shown to send apostles, and shown to authenticate the New Testament witness as continuous with earlier Scripture. The body of writings so treated has been identified, recognized, grounded, exhibited as one testimony, distinguished as to operations, warranted as inspired record, shown not to fail as record, and synthesized as the written Word of the God who cannot lie. That written Word has been heard in a particular controversy: John 10:34–36, the Dedication scene, the blasphemy-charge, the appeal to what is written in their law. The writing so cited has been heard in its own argument: Psalm 82, the judicial address, “I have said, Ye are gods,” those to whom the word of God came. The reasoning from that writing has been followed: the a fortiori, the court, the weight of the written text as settling-material. The exact statement that made the lesser case non-negotiable has been examined: “the scripture cannot be broken”; “broken” as the loosing of the writing’s force so as to evacuate the appeal. Why that statement is true of the writing has been examined: because the Graphē is God’s truthful written Word, such that its force as court cannot be loosed without denying what it is. His saying it is the assertion. The why is the doctrine of the writing. The dedicated identification of that Word as truth has been examined: “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” The Word belonging to the Father is truth. Sanctification through truth is through that Word because that Word is truth. The conclusion earned by that preceding argument has now been drawn: the Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. The Graphē-gate is in force. Movement VIII is complete.

The writings that present that rank do not leave unused the further question of mishandling. The writing has been ranked as primary written measure. A ranked writing still leaves the dedicated distinction in which the authority of the text is held apart from the fallibility of the interpreter. The next necessary question is therefore not a new curiosity. It is the question the locked assignment names:

> **How is the authority of Scripture to be distinguished from the authority of interpretation, now that the Graphē has been shown to be the primary written authority, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that distinction rather than a second gate, and rather than a finished labour-file?**

That is the subject of:

# Chapter 66 — Authority of Scripture Versus Authority of Interpretation

> **Distinguish the authority of the text from the fallibility of the interpreter.**

The investigation now moves from:

> **the Graphē as primary written authority**
>
> to:
>
> **when authoritative truth is mishandled.**

# End of Chapter 65

title: Authority of Scripture Versus Authority of Interpretation
body:
> **Movement IX — When Authoritative Truth Is Mishandled**

> **Central objective:** Distinguish the authority of the text from the fallibility of the interpreter — the Graphē’s standing as primary written authority from a reader’s or community’s claim about what the text means — so that an authoritative truthful writing is not converted into a grant that every interpretation of it is authoritative, and so that the fallibility of readers is not converted into a grant that all readings are equal. This opens Movement IX. It is not Chapter 65 retried as a second gate, not Chapter 57 retried as a second infallibility-file, not Chapter 58’s foreshadow rewritten as the dedicated distinction, not a catalog of specific misreadings, not a treatment of theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution as systems, not a finished account of secondary sources becoming primary, and not Chapters 70–73, Movement X, or the First Principles written in advance.

---

## Chapter Assignment

Chapter 65 established Movement VIII’s last word. The Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived — the decisive written measure among written authorities, not merely one religious book among equals, not subordinate to later tradition or institution as a higher court, not interchangeable with every later claim about the text. “Primary” named firstness among written measures. It did not name the non-existence of other writings, the infallibility of interpreters, a blank check for tradition, or the end of the book. The gate-file is already in force. Movement VIII is complete. Movement IX now opens.

Chapter 65 ended by naming the next necessary question, not a new curiosity:

> **How is the authority of Scripture to be distinguished from the authority of interpretation, now that the Graphē has been shown to be the primary written authority, and now that the next file’s first word is to be that distinction rather than a second gate, and rather than a finished labour-file?**

That is this chapter’s assignment.

The locked Table of Contents states the work in one sentence:

> **Distinguish the authority of the text from the fallibility of the interpreter.**

The locked knowledge-flow places this distinction after the Graphē as primary written authority and before the dedicated examination of how Scripture is misread. The locked guidance states the same sequence as a governing rule of the whole investigation: the hermeneutical question — once we have an authoritative truthful text, how do we correctly understand it? — is distinct from establishing the authority of the text. The authority of Scripture does not make every interpretation of Scripture authoritative. Scriptural authority is not interpretive infallibility of the reader. Understanding is not authority over the text. God’s Word is not every human claim made about God’s Word. Those core distinctions have already been named as architecture. The present file is their dedicated opening as Movement IX’s first word. It does not re-prove that the Graphē is the primary written authority. It cites Chapter 65 as established. It does not re-answer why the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. It cites Chapter 57 as established. It does not re-synthesize Movement VII. It cites Chapter 58 as established. It does not re-try the John 10 arc, the identification of the Father’s word as truth, corpus, recognition, inspiration’s guarantees, or the lexical establishment of γραφή. It cites those files as established. It does not catalogue the species of misreading. It does not write Chapter 67. It does not treat theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution as finished systems. It does not write Chapter 68. It does not finish the account of secondary sources becoming primary. It does not write Chapter 69. It does not write tergiversation, accepted heresies, aridity, or *apeiros*. It does not write Movement X. It does not enter the First Principles. It performs the distinction without which Movement IX would possess a ranked writing and still lack the first word that ranked writing forces: the writing’s standing is not the interpreter’s standing.

A ranked writing, now controlled as the Graphē’s firstness among written measures, still leaves a further question. If this writing is the primary written authority, does that standing migrate into the reader, the office, the community, or the later claim that says what the writing means? If it migrates automatically, the gate was a blank check. If it migrates never, even when a reading states what the writing actually communicates, knowledge of the writing has been denied. Naming neighbourhood is not drawing the distinction. The present file is that distinction, at the level the premises warrant, and not beyond it.

The remaining question of the book’s sequence follows. Sequence continues the investigation. It does not convert the present line into hesitation.

---

## Central Objective

> **To distinguish, from the biblical record and from premises already in force, the authority of Scripture from the authority of interpretation, so that Movement IX’s first word is one inspectable verdict: the Graphē’s standing as primary written authority does not transfer automatically to a reader’s or community’s claim about what the text means; the fallibility of the interpreter is compatible with the infallibility of the record; an authoritative truthful text does not make every interpretation of it authoritative, and the fact that readers err does not make all readings equal; to keep this distinction distinct from a catalog of specific misreadings, from a treatment of theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution as systems, and from a finished account of secondary sources becoming primary; to refuse the reductions that say “Scripture is authoritative, therefore my reading is,” that say “all readings are equal because readers err,” or that treat this chapter as already Chapters 67–73; and to refuse both under-claim and over-claim.**

The governing movement is:

> **Gate-file already stated → question of two authorities that must not be collapsed → the two objects defined at this stage → objects distinguished → premises already in force used, not retried → one clean account of sequence and limits → authority of Scripture, interpretation, and authority of interpretation defined → why the two must remain distinct → transfer and despair named as the two live failures → positive warrant from the gate, from the record’s non-failure, from the ranking “God true, every man a liar,” and from the writing as court of later speech → biblical record of the distinction in use → required distinctions → competing reductions refused → inspectable inference → warranted conclusion → Movement IX opened → sequence to how Scripture is misread.**

The chapter’s conclusion is affirmative:

> **The authority of Scripture and the authority of interpretation are two objects. The Graphē stands as the primary written authority already earned. A reader’s or community’s claim about what that writing means is a later act of stating sense. The writing’s standing does not transfer automatically to that later act. Fallibility of the reader is compatible with infallibility of the record. An authoritative truthful text does not make every interpretation of it authoritative. The fact that readers err does not make all readings equal. A correct reading states what the writing communicates; it does not become a second Graphē. An incorrect reading remains incorrect; it does not become the writing by quoting the writing, by occupying an office, or by gathering a community. This opens Movement IX. It is not Chapter 67. It is not Chapters 68–73. It is not Movement X. That is this chapter’s conclusion, stated here with full force.**

The remaining questions follow by sequence. The verdict is already in force as warranted distinction, not as postponed guesswork.

---

# 66.1 The Question Created by the Preceding Chapter

Movement VIII is complete. John 10:34–36 has been examined as a complete argument in the Dedication controversy: an appeal to what is written as decisive in a dispute over blasphemy. Psalm 82 has been examined as the cited writing’s own argument. The reasoning from that wording has been followed: the Graphē as court, not decoration. The exact statement has been examined: οὐ δύναται λυθῆναι ἡ γραφή; “broken,” as λυθῆναι functions there, is the loosing of the writing’s force as court so as to evacuate the appeal. Why that incapacity belongs to the writing has been answered: because the Graphē is God’s truthful written Word, such that its force as court cannot be loosed without denying what it is. The Father’s word has been identified as truth. The conclusion earned by that preceding argument has been drawn: the Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. The Graphē-gate is in force. Movement VIII’s last assigned word has been stated.

Chapter 65 established the gate-file. That conclusion is a premise here. A ranked writing still leaves a further question: if the Graphē is the primary written authority, how is that standing to be held apart from the standing a reader, teacher, office, or community claims for a statement of what the writing means? Rank names the writing as measure. The present file draws the distinction that rank requires once the measure is in later hands.

A people can receive the Dedication scene as a controversy, receive “cannot be broken” as unloosenable standing, receive “thy word is truth” as identification, receive the Graphē as primary written authority, and still collapse the writing into the later claim that says what the writing means. The writings themselves force the further analysis. He has treated the writing as court against His hearers. He has said they err, not knowing the scriptures. He has opened understanding that they might understand writings that already stood. Apostles have named wresting of writings that already stand. Hearers have searched the scriptures whether an apostolic sermon were so. The God who cannot lie has made known. The record does not fail as what it actually communicates. Those sentences, already in force, have a joint consequence concerning two objects that must not be collapsed. If they have none, “authority of Scripture versus authority of interpretation” is a title. If they have every consequence a later slogan wishes — a catalog of misreadings finished now, tradition examined as a system now, secondary sources finished as a displacement-file now — the investigation has stopped reasoning.

The question is therefore not:

> **Why is the Graphē the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived?**

That question has been answered.

The question is:

> **How is the authority of Scripture to be distinguished from the authority of interpretation — the writing’s standing from the fallibility of the interpreter — now that the writing has been ranked as primary written measure, and not as a second gate, and not as a later catalog of misreadings?**

If Movement IX proceeded from the gate to a catalog of misreadings without drawing this distinction, it would skip the locked step. If it treated this file as already Chapter 67, it would consume the species of error before the two objects have been named as two. If it treated this file as a retry of Chapter 65, it would convert a distinction-file into a second gate-file. If it treated this file as a rewrite of Chapter 57 or Chapter 58, it would convert Movement IX’s opening into a second Movement VII limit. If it treated this file as already Chapters 68–73, it would close the movement’s later questions inside its first word. The present file is the dedicated distinction between the authority of the text and the fallibility of the interpreter.

That is a different operation from piety. It is the operation this chapter must perform.

---

# 66.2 What This Chapter Does Not Repeat

Chapters 1–3 established truth as conformity to reality, distinct from belief, popularity, institutional consensus, and sincerity as a determinant of truth. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the opening ontology of truth. It uses truth as already defined, now as the object the writing measures and as the object a later claim about the writing may or may not state.

Chapters 4–7 established knowledge, evidence, reason, and rational warrant as inspectable operations. Chapter 8 raised the problem of ultimate authority. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the opening epistemology. It uses reason as already defined, now as the standard against which the distinction is examined as a join of established doctrine, and it uses Chapter 8 as the problem a ranked writing still leaves when later speakers claim the writing’s standing for their own speech.

Chapters 10–12 established that God is the ground of truth, that He is truthful, faithful, and immutable, and that falsehood is incompatible with Him. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-write the impossibility of divine falsehood. It uses that impossibility as source-side ground of the ranking: God true; the interpreter, as man, not thereby true.

Chapters 14 established the problem with human accounts about God: later speech about God is not God, and is not God’s Word merely by being speech about God. That conclusion remains a premise. This chapter does not re-write that file. It uses it: a claim about what Scripture means is a human account about the writing, and is therefore to be tested by the writing, not received as a second writing.

Chapters 20–22 established γραφή (*graphē*, G1124) as writing that, in biblical usage, designates Holy Writ / Scripture. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try the lexical files. It uses them: the Graphē is the written object whose standing is one thing; a later sentence about that writing is another written or spoken object.

Chapters 30–31, 56–57 established inspiration, “all Scripture,” inspiration’s guarantees, and why the record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. Chapter 57 already distinguished infallibility of the record from infallibility of the interpreter, and record from interpretation, as limits of that verdict. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try the infallibility-file. It uses the distinction Chapter 57 required as a limit and now examines as Movement IX’s first dedicated object.

Chapter 58 synthesized truth, authority, and the written Word, and named that authority of the written Word is not infallibility of interpreters as the shape of that synthesis. That conclusion remains a premise. This chapter does not re-try the synthesis. It uses the foreshadow as a premise of the dedicated distinction.

Chapters 59–65 established Christ’s verdict on the Graphē and the gate that the Graphē is the primary written authority. Chapter 65 already refused to confer that standing upon every later quotation, and reserved Movement IX as the dedicated examination. Those conclusions remain premises. This chapter does not re-try the gate. It uses the gate as the ranked object now in later hands.

This chapter does not recatalogue Romans 3:4 as if the ranking “God true, every man a liar” were still in doubt as a sentence. It does not treat 2 Peter 1:20–21 as a second production-file. It does not invent unverifiable details of a later council-chamber, a reconstructed imprimatur-office, a named extra-biblical school-quarrel, or a weather-report of a particular pulpit as the chapter’s center. The new function is this:

> **To distinguish the authority of the text from the fallibility of the interpreter; to refuse both emptiness and overclaim; and to leave the catalog of misreadings, the system-files, the displacement-file, the later Movement IX pathologies, labour, and the First Principles in their assigned files.**

---

# 66.3 Define the Question: Two Authorities That Must Not Be Collapsed

**Authority of Scripture versus authority of interpretation**, in this chapter, is the dedicated account of two objects that neighbourhood invites us to treat as one: the Graphē’s standing as primary written authority, already earned, and the standing a reader or community claims for a statement of what that writing means.

The phrase is easily abused. In ordinary speech “authority of interpretation” may mean that interpretation is illegitimate, that every reading is as binding as the text, that no reading can be known to be correct, that an office is a second Graphē, that a community’s consensus is the writing’s living voice, that this chapter is already a catalog of errors, or that this chapter is already the labour of rightly dividing. None of those senses is this chapter’s object.

Four elements belong to the definition.

First, **two objects**. The writing is one object. The later act of stating what the writing means is another. Collapse of the two is the error this chapter exists to refuse. Separation of the two into a despair that no meaning can be reached is the opposite error this chapter also exists to refuse.

Second, **authority as standing, used of each object in its own place**. “Authority of Scripture” names the Graphē’s already-earned standing as primary written measure. “Authority of interpretation” names the standing claimed for a later statement of sense — claimed by a reader, a teacher, an office, a school, a tradition, or a community. The second standing is not, by being claimed, the first standing.

Third, **fallibility of the interpreter as compatible with infallibility of the record**. The reader may err. The record does not fail as what it actually communicates. Compatibility is the doctrine. Transfer of non-failure from record to reader is not the doctrine. Despair of all reading because readers can err is not the doctrine.

Fourth, **not those other claims**. The definition excludes, as not this object: a retry of Chapter 65; a rewrite of Chapter 57 or Chapter 58; a catalog of specific misreadings; a treatment of theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution as systems; a finished account of secondary sources becoming primary; tergiversation, accepted heresies, aridity, and *apeiros* as finished files; Movement X’s labour-files; the First Principles as this file’s achievement. Those exclusions are part of the definition. They are not a later apology.

Thus:

> **The question of this chapter is not why the Graphē is the primary written authority, why the record does not fail, or how later readers commit the several species of misreading. Those questions have been examined or remain later. The question is how the authority of the text is to be distinguished from the fallibility of the interpreter in the sense just defined.**

# 66.4 Distinguish Ten Objects That Must Not Be Collapsed

The investigation fails at the first step if it treats different objects as one.

## 66.4.1 This distinction and Chapter 65’s gate

This chapter distinguishes the writing’s standing from the interpreter’s standing. Chapter 65 drew the conclusion that the Graphē is the primary written authority. Gate and distinction neighbour one another. They are not the same file. To treat this file as already Chapter 65 retried would hide the distinction inside a second gate. To omit the distinction in order to protect the gate would leave the gate unjoined to the first word Movement IX assigns. The gate remains premise. The distinction is the new object.

## 66.4.2 This distinction and Chapter 57’s record-versus-interpreter limit

Chapter 57 established that the inspired scriptural record does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates, and required already that infallibility of the record is not infallibility of the interpreter. Limit of a verdict is not the dedicated distinction-file. To treat this file as Chapter 57 rewritten would collapse two movements. To ignore Chapter 57 would pretend that compatibility of a fallible reader with a non-failing record had never been named. The limit remains premise. The dedicated distinction is now the object.

## 66.4.3 This distinction and Chapter 58’s foreshadow

Chapter 58 named that authority of the written Word is not infallibility of interpreters as the shape of Movement VII’s fourth member, and reserved Chapter 66 as the dedicated file. Foreshadow is not performance. To treat this file as Chapter 58 rewritten would convert an opening into a second synthesis. To ignore Chapter 58 would pretend that the synthesis had never required the distinction. Foreshadow remains premise. Performance is now the object.

## 66.4.4 Authority of Scripture and authority of interpretation

The writing’s standing is one object. The standing claimed for a later statement of what the writing means is another. The whole chapter exists because those objects are two. Naming them as two is not yet a catalog of the ways the second object fails.

## 66.4.5 This chapter and a catalog of misreadings

Chapter 67 examines errors arising from poor perception, deficient understanding, faulty inference, context failure, or improper handling of the text. Those are later questions. The present file must already refuse to treat every reading as the text. Refusal is not the catalog written now.

Chapter 68 examines secondary intellectual and institutional systems in relation to the Graphē. None becomes primary authority merely by claiming Christian identity, academic status, antiquity, or institutional recognition. Those are later questions. The present file must already refuse to confer the writing’s standing upon a system as system. Refusal is not that system-file written now.

Chapter 69 examines what happens when commentaries, traditions, institutions, teachers, systems, or experiences govern the meaning of Scripture instead of serving under it. Those are later questions. Chapters 70–73 examine tergiversation, accepted heresies, aridity, and *apeiros*. Those are later questions. The present file is the movement’s first word, not the movement’s last word under another name.

Movement X asks how the Graphē is to be laboured in: scholarly impetus, perception, reasoning, quotation and knowledge, *spoudazō*, exercise, maturity, rightly dividing, the approved workman, the discipline of interpretation, readiness for the First Principles. Those are later questions. The distinction names why later labour has an object that remains the measure of the labourer. It does not perform the labour-files.

Hebrews 5:12–6:3 and the six First Principles remain later. The reconstructible proposition that the Graphē is the premiere convention for hearing from God belongs here only as coherence with the writing as measure of later claims, not as the First Principles consumed. The distinction is foundation for later entry. It is not a seventh principle invented in this file.
